title: Percentage Change, Reverse Percentages and Simple Interest
seo_title: Year 8 Percentage Change Worksheets: Multipliers, Reverse Percentages and Simple Interest
standard_code: KS3: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
standard_text: Solve problems involving percentage change, including: percentage increase, decrease and original value problems and simple interest in financial mathematics.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 percentage change worksheets: increase and decrease with multipliers, find the percentage change, reverse percentages to find the original amount, and simple interest. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Increase by 15%: × 1.15. Decrease by 15%: × 0.85. Percentage change = change ÷ original × 100.
key_sub: To find the original amount, divide by the multiplier: £68 after 15% off → 68 ÷ 0.85 = £80.
body_html:
How it works

A multiplier does a percentage change in one step: increase by 15% → × 1.15; decrease by 15% → × 0.85.

Percentage change = change ÷ original × 100.

Reverse percentage: if the new amount is 85% of the original, divide by 0.85 to find the original.

Simple interest is the same amount every year: interest = principal × rate × years.

Example

Increase £240 by 17.5%.

Multiplier 1.175.

1.175 × 240 = 282.

Answer: £282

Example

A price rises from £80 to £92. Find the percentage increase.

Change = 12.

12 ÷ 80 × 100 = 15.

Answer: 15%

Example

After 20% off, a bag costs £36. Find the original price.

£36 is 80%.

36 ÷ 0.8 = 45.

Answer: £45

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the new amount when finding a percentage change. Always divide by the original.
  • Stopping at the change: a 15% increase on £240 is £276, not £36.
  • Adding the percentage back on to undo a discount: 20% off then +20% does not return to the original.
  • Using 0.15 instead of 1.15 to increase by 15%.

faq.q: How do I calculate percentage change?
faq.a: Find the difference, divide by the original amount and multiply by 100.
The decimal you multiply by to make a percentage change in one step. A 20% increase is × 1.2 and a 20% decrease is × 0.8.

faq.q: How do I find the original price after a discount?
faq.a: Work out what percentage is left, write it as a decimal and divide. After 30% off, £56 ÷ 0.7 = £80.
Interest that is the same every year, worked out on the original amount: principal × rate × number of years.
